findings.text: The pair brackets guest-origin interrupt handling on a virtual CPU. The entry hook records the incoming interrupt kind into the field handling_intr_from_guest, while the exit hook clears that field to show no such interrupt remains in flight. Stores use single-copy atomic visibility so concurrent readers observe a coherent marker.

The loader installs the active paging root into the virtual machine control block. When nested paging is enabled it programs the nested table base, flags nested paging state dirty, informs hypervisor tracking of the translation root, and reloads the guest control register value for the saved paging base; otherwise it installs either an encrypted root combined with the active process-context identifier for wide paging mode or the raw root for narrow mode, warning if a context identifier is unexpectedly present in narrow mode. In all cases the saved paging-base register is updated and control-register state is marked dirty.
The patcher overwrites the start of a caller-supplied buffer with the fixed encoding of the virtualization vendor call instruction, providing the guest hypercall trampoline for this backend.
Support for supervisor-mode execution protection under nested paging is reported directly from a host-wide capability flag, independent of the particular virtual machine instance passed in.

Emulation support is denied for the machine-check extended control register and for the range reserved for the other vendor virtualization feature registers, while the system-management base register is allowed only when system-management support is compiled in and, on confidential-computing hosts, only for guests that do not use encrypted register state; all other indices are treated as emulated.

After guest capability bits are updated, the backend reconciles features that lack fine-grained control. It forces the extended save variant to match the combination of host support and guest save enablement so that extended supervisor state is context-switched on transitions, drops the virtual save-load feature for guests that report an incompatible vendor identity to allow emulation of system-call register clearing, and delegates additional fixups to confidential-computing handling for secure guests.

If the extended save variant is left disabled in bookkeeping while the guest can still execute it, the supervisor state register would not be switched across transitions, leaking host values into the guest and vice versa. The forced-enable reconciliation above closes that exposure.
The backend always reports that write-back cache invalidation causes a virtualization exit.

The mapping entry pairs a vendor exit code with a pipeline stage indicating whether interception is evaluated before exception delivery, after exception delivery, or after memory access. Helper constructors build entries for each stage class.

A static table translates generic instruction intercepts into vendor exit codes plus stages. Most control, debug, descriptor, virtualization, timer, and input-output operations are handled late in the pipeline, a smaller set of control-flow and system instructions is handled early, and the monitor wait hint is handled after memory access.

The checker decides whether an emulated instruction should be reflected to the outer hypervisor as a nested exit. It rejects unknown intercept kinds and stage mismatches by allowing emulation to continue; otherwise it materializes vendor exit information into the control block, including next-instruction location when the host provides that feature, and consults nested-exit handling to choose between reporting interception and continuing emulation. Specializations adjust the exit code for control-register selection, debug-register indexing, direction of model-specific register access, pause prefix qualification, and input-output width and addressing.

While interrupts remain disabled after an exit, the handler forwards machine-check exits to machine-check handling and marks the virtual CPU as sitting at an instruction boundary for interrupt exits; all other exit codes are ignored at this stage.
Machine-check setup constrains the advertised capability mask to the architecturally defined low portion, clearing reserved high bits.

System-management interrupt admission refuses delivery while a nested entry is pending or while management interrupts are blocked, and refuses injection into a nested guest when that condition is configured to cause an exit; otherwise it permits delivery.

Management-mode transitions preserve nested execution. Entry has no effect unless the CPU is in nested mode, in which case outer-host state is spilled to the host save area and a marker records nested origin; exit has no effect unless that marker and long-mode support are present, in which case restoration requires vendor support, virtualization enablement, and successful validation of cached control state, otherwise re-entry is abandoned and a pending nested entry is recorded only on success.

Legacy management save format does not preserve extended feature and virtualization state, and the primary control structure is reused during management mode, so outer-host state would be lost without the explicit spill and restore via the host save area; incorrect handling there corrupts the outer host or the nested guest.

When waiting for a management-interrupt window, the backend arms the start-interrupt interception if global interrupts are disabled and virtual interrupt support is present, so that enabling interrupts causes an exit; if global interrupts are already enabled it relies on the upcoming return-from-management exit and arms nothing.
Delivery of initialization signals from the local interrupt controller is considered blocked whenever global interrupt flag state is clear.

Startup inter-processor interrupt delivery programs the code-segment selector and base from the supplied vector and resets the instruction pointer to the start of the branch stub for ordinary guests, while guests with encrypted register state are diverted to a confidential-computing delivery path.

Virtual-machine lifecycle composes several subsystems. Initialization prepares confidential-computing state, disables pause exits when pause filtering is turned off, and prepares speculation-defence state; destruction tears down interrupt virtualization, confidential computing, and speculation-defence state. In this configuration the confidential-computing init and destroy helpers are no-ops, and disabling exits accumulates a mask into per-machine disabled-exit state.
Allocation of the virtual interrupt-controller backing store obtains a confidential-safe page and returns its kernel-visible address, reporting failure with a null pointer when allocation fails.

The backend publishes a static operations vector that binds virtualization lifecycle, register and descriptor access, paging and cache flushing, exit handling, injection and windows, nested and management-mode transitions, and interrupt-virtualization hooks to local implementations, leaving the emulated-instruction update hook empty and declaring split destination handling for extended interrupt-controller commands.

Programming a paging root for narrow mode while a process-context identifier remains active is treated as unexpected and triggers a warning, since context identifiers should be impossible there; the raw root is still installed.

The spill path assumes the control-block save area starts at a fixed architecturally defined offset within the block and within the host save page, enforced at build time; the copy preserves outer-host state that would otherwise be clobbered by management-mode reuse.
